evals.prompt: Start two Codex workers in cmux panes for this repository: one to inspect the API tests and one to inspect the CLI tests. Give each worker a narrow scope, keep the panes visible, and tell me how to send a follow-up prompt.
evals.expected_output: Uses codex-peer-sessions, chooses pane placement, launches named workers with safe Codex flags, records fleet metadata, and explains pane relay limitations.

evals.prompt: Create a persistent Codex thread in /home/me/dev, ask it for a read-only migration risk report, and return the thread ID plus the final answer as JSON.
evals.expected_output: Uses codex-thread.py, starts or resumes a named non-ephemeral thread with read-only sandboxing, waits for turn/completed, and returns the thread ID and machine-readable reply.

evals.prompt: The Codex peer fleet looks frozen. Check the worker panes, distinguish an approval prompt from a completed worker, and stop only the fleet workers without killing my other Codex sessions.
evals.expected_output: Reads the fleet metadata and panes, reports uncertainty when screen output is incomplete, kills only exact recorded worker PIDs, closes matching cmux surfaces, and avoids pkill codex.

evals.prompt: Start three visible Codex workers in Herdr for this repository without adding panes to my coordinator workspace. Name them by responsibility so I can distinguish them in the workspace and agent lists.
evals.expected_output: Creates one named fleet workspace, places all three workers inside it with descriptive pane and agent labels, preserves the coordinator workspace, records stable pane IDs, and prints one fleet-workspace cleanup command.
